subject: Request: Community credits for JanusLib workshop series
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@januslib.org>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: [JanusLib] Request: community credits for workshop series

Hi Chloe,

Hope you're well — I'm Samir, one of the maintainers at JanusLib. We're running a four-part community workshop series in Q1 to help projects migrate to modern embeddings + retrieval. We've seen a lot of interest from maintainers who sign up via your PLG flow, and we'd like to request a one-off promotional credit package to cover staging + demo usage for the cohort.

The ask: 200k free token credits (self-serve credits applied to a JanusLib team account) plus a 3-month trial extension for projects created through the workshop landing page. The credits will be used for demo runs, automated tests during sessions, and to provide invited maintainers a frictionless demo experience.

Attached is a short request doc with the workshop schedule and expected attendee list. We're also partnering with Open Source Fund (cc'd) who may help promote.

Can you advise the process and whether Redwood can authorize this program? Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if helpful.

Thanks —
Samir
Samir Patel
Core Maintainer, JanusLib
samir@januslib.org

Subject: Re: Fwd: [JanusLib] Request: community credits for workshop series

Thanks Chloe — I reviewed the attachments and the ask looks aligned with our PLG community grant intents. A couple of operational notes before we sign off:

1) Cap per-project: let's limit to 25k tokens per individual project created via their landing page (so the 200k total can cover ~8 projects as they scale). This prevents a single team from draining the allocation.
2) Trial extension: approve a 3-month extension for accounts created through the campaign, but mark accounts flagged as suspicious for manual review.
3) Tracking: require a query parameter in the signup link so we can attribute usage and measure activation. Chloe — please get them to add ?utm_campaign=janus-workshops to the signups.
4) Legal/terms: no additional contract required; treat as a marketing promo. If they request invoiced credits or longer-term reserved capacity, escalate to Sales.

I approve the promotional allocation from the community credits pool. I'll mark this in the internal tracker and allocate the token bucket. Chloe — can you confirm we have the HubSpot record and I'll push the allocation?

—Marcus

Hi Samir / Ellen — great to connect. Good news: we can authorize a one-off promotional allocation for the JanusLib workshop cohort. High-level terms below:

- Allocation: 200,000 free token credits to be applied to the JanusLib team account on signups attributed to their workshop landing page.
- Per-project cap: 25,000 tokens per created project (enforced via promo redemptions).
- Trial extension: 3-month trial extension for accounts created through the campaign.
- Attribution: require ?utm_campaign=janus-workshops (or equivalent HubSpot parameter) in the signup link.
- Tracking: Redwood will provide weekly redemption counts for the duration of the allocation.
- Validity window: credits available for signups from 2027-01-05 through 2027-04-05.

Next steps for JanusLib:
1) Confirm the landing page URL and ensure the UTM parameter is present.
2) Share the HubSpot company record or we can create a simple tracking token.
3) Confirm a primary contact for operational questions (Samir noted Ellen from Open Source Fund).

Marcus will allocate the promo bucket and Lauren will log the promo in the registry. I'll follow up with a short mutual action plan and the redemption link to paste into your landing page.

If you'd like a brief call tomorrow to walk through implementation, I'm available 11:00–12:00 PT.

Cheers —
